thread:
Maria: Heads-up — onboarding Lattice9b int4 shows steady-state memory climb over long sessions, not just coldstart OOMs. Repro on canary with long chats (~30 turns).
Ajay: can you paste the alloc graph / gc logs?
Maria: quick snippet: `gpu_mem_used: 18.3GB -> 21.9GB` after ~12 turns, then keeps inching up. No obvious KV growth.
Tyler: any difference between prefetch on vs off?
Maria: toggled prefetch off, still climbs but a bit slower. Prefetch on + cwnd=4 is the worst.
Sophia: hmm. could be slot fragmentation in the runtime. Did you run the slot compactor stats?
Maria: ran `slotctl stats` on the canary: active_slots 96, fragmented_slots ~18%, free_contig_low=1.5GB
Ajay: that low contiguous free sounds like repeated small kv allocations. Is max_new_tokens large in tests?
Maria: defaults to 512 for these QA runs. We also tried 256 — slope reduced but still trending up.
Tyler: try forcing max_new_tokens=128 and cwnd=2, see steady state?
Maria: did that: steady at ~19.1GB after warmup, flat for 20 turns. So smaller max_new_tokens helped.
Sophia: ok that suggests allocation pressure from larger generation windows. But why fragmentation persists? two hypotheses: (1) KV cache per turn isn't fully freed because of session pinning bug, (2) kernel allocator isn't coalescing freed pages under certain quantized paths.
Ajay: can you share a trace of `alloc_fragmenter` when it happens? Also run with `--kernel-debug=alloc` for a single session.
Maria: posting small trace excerpt: ```ALLOC_TRACE session=abc123 turn=13 alloc 64MB slot#12; free slot#5 32MB; alloc 48MB slot#5 -> split; compaction skipped;```
Tyler: compaction skipped — that's a clue. Is compactor threshold set too high for int4 path? There's a runtime flag `--compactor-threshold-percent` (default 30). If fragmented below threshold it won't compact.
Sophia: can we lower to 10 for the canary roll? Tradeoff is compaction CPU. But this model is latency-sensitive. Maybe do adaptive: lower threshold only when session length > 20 turns.
Ajay: quick patch: runtime change to `if session_turns>20 and frag_percent>10 then compact`. I'll run a canary with that + max_new_tokens=128 and cwnd=2.
Maria: canary results (20 sessions x 40 turns): no steady climb, fragmentation drops from 18% -> 6% after compaction and stays flat, 99th latency +6ms.
Tyler: +6ms seems acceptable vs OOM risk. Need perf regression test in CI.
Sophia: also add a guard: if quant path uses small-page kernels, reduce sustained compaction frequency to avoid extra CPU.
Maria: created a small rollout plan in the canary config: `compactor.adaptive=true, compactor.threshold=10, max_new_tokens.default=128, cwnd.default=2` and added a canary gate for quality evals.
Ajay: ping infra-bot to provision a 5-node canary with metrics retention 48h.
infra-bot: provisioning canary cluster "lattice9b-int4-fragfix-canary" (5 nodes) — ETA 4m. :gear:
Maria: thanks. I'll collect memory traces + evals after 2h and post summary.
Tyler: also add a regression alert if steady-state mem > 20GB for 15m during canary.
Sophia: good. If canary is clean, we can ship as opt-in flag for Dedicated customers first. Then decide default.
Maria: notes for postmortem: root cause likely alloc coalescing + compactor threshold being too conservative for long-turn chats on int4 kernels. Mitigation: adaptive compaction + lower max_new_tokens default for this model.
Ajay: sounds solid. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
